title: Control one complete conversion segment without a fibre-gap loss
statement: After exact binding absorption, reference and actual internal rates coincide and conversion intensities are b_e and r_e b_e with fixed r_e in[1-eta,1+eta],eta<=1/2 (eta<=8Ddelta for delta<=1/(16D)). Start from the SAME arbitrary enabled fine state and stop at first conversion sigma. The local activation lemma gives finite stopping moments under both laws; the preconversion fibre is finite, justifying localized likelihood removal. Retain EVERY holding time, binding/release mark, final conversion label and resulting fine state. The reference compensator gives E_ref integral_0^sigma sum_e b_e dt=1, even if b vanishes at intermediate states. Exact stopped-path entropy is KL(P_ref||P_actual)=E_ref integral sum_e b_e(r_e-1-log r_e)dt<=2eta². Pinsker yields TV<=eta, also for any projected next-mark/fine/decoded state. This is uniform in n, fibre speed, initial fine state and number of internal marks, with no point-weight or gap loss. TV controls bounded observables; polynomial time/firing rewards require the separately paid moment/truncation estimates. Repeated segment errors can accumulate, and event-stationary occupation weights require recurrence control; no time-uniform coupling or stationary compiler follows. Hoessly-Wiuf-Xia Cambridge2026 Theorem2 assumes complex balance AND stationarity of the conditional reduced law; independent conversion errors do not automatically satisfy either import. No division by a possibly zero conversion intensity is allowed.
